symptom_investigations.symptom_description:
Симптом: высокая загрузка CPU процессами PostgreSQL. pg_profile показывает CPU через
pg_stat_kcache (top_rusage_statements) и active_time на уровне БД.

causes.title: Доминирующие SQL по CPU (pg_stat_kcache)
causes.description: Несколько запросов потребляют большую долю user/system CPU за интервал.
evidence: [nt1] Топ CPU: sum_cpu_time=23229.9s, user_time_pct=31.9%
[nt1] hex=e2a55c68949e5d1e: select v1_0.object_id from statecontracts.t_value v1_0 where v1_0.inn is not nul…
[nt1] #2: sum_cpu_time=14123.0s hex=d5e326dff67d955a
[nt1] #3: sum_cpu_time=13030.6s hex=7e5e1a652457d8db
[nt2] Топ CPU: sum_cpu_time=27442.2s, user_time_pct=33.1%
[nt2] hex=e2a55c68949e5d1e: select v1_0.object_id from statecontracts.t_value v1_0 where v1_0.inn is not nul…
[nt2] #2: sum_cpu_time=15140.6s hex=7e5e1a652457d8db
[nt2] #3: sum_cpu_time=14619.5s hex=d5e326dff67d955a
[nt3] Топ CPU: sum_cpu_time=28124.9s, user_time_pct=33.1%
[nt3] hex=e2a55c68949e5d1e: select v1_0.object_id from statecontracts.t_value v1_0 where v1_0.inn is not nul…
[nt3] #2: sum_cpu_time=15448.9s hex=7e5e1a652457d8db
[nt3] #3: sum_cpu_time=15177.8s hex=d5e326dff67d955a
confirm_actions: EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) для топ-3 SQL по sum_cpu_time из отчёта
Проверить, совпадает ли пик CPU на OS с интервалом отчёта pg_profile
refute_actions: Если sum_cpu_time топ-запросов <5% интервала — CPU уходит не в SQL (фон, autovacuum, checkpoint)
Сравнить топ CPU между двумя периодами: запрос исчез из топа — не корневая причина текущего пика

causes.title: Checkpoint / bgwriter / IO wait в kernel CPU
causes.description: Высокий system_time, checkpoint write, maxwritten_clean — kernel CPU на запись.
evidence: [nt1] checkpoints_req=56, checkpoint_write_time=25187.0s
[nt2] checkpoints_req=39, checkpoint_write_time=38898.3s
[nt3] checkpoints_req=30, checkpoint_write_time=39318.4s
confirm_actions: Сопоставить system_time_pct в top_rusage с WAL/checkpoint метриками
refute_actions: checkpoints_req низкий и checkpoint_write_time мал — не checkpoint

causes.title: Autovacuum / analyze во время нагрузки
causes.description: Bloat, stale vacuum, высокий mods/dead_pct — autovacuum конкурирует за CPU.
evidence: [nt1] Bloat: pgse_profile.sample_statements dead_pct=10.15296960859762%
[nt2] Bloat: pgse_profile.sample_stat_tables dead_pct=16.536570289395474%
confirm_actions: pg_stat_activity: autovacuum workers в пик CPU
refute_actions: Нет таблиц с высоким dead_pct и autovacuum свежий — маловероятно

causes.title: Параллельные запросы / max_parallel_workers
causes.description: Много parallel workers увеличивают суммарный CPU.
confirm_actions: EXPLAIN: Gather / Parallel Seq Scan в топ SQL
refute_actions: Планы без parallel nodes при высоком CPU — ищите другие причины

causes.title: JIT-компиляция запросов
causes.description: JIT включён и топ SQL имеет заметный jit_total_time.
confirm_actions: Проверить jit_* поля в top_statements для медленных/тяжёлых запросов
Сравнить plan time vs exec time; jit_generation_time в pg_profile
Тест с SET jit=off для подозрительного запроса на НТ
refute_actions: jit_total_time отсутствует или << total_exec_time — JIT не доминирует

causes.title: TLB pressure без HugePages (большой shared_buffers)
causes.description:
При большом shared_buffers и huge_pages=try/off растёт system CPU из‑за TLB miss.
Postgres Pro рекомендует huge pages для крупных shared memory сегментов.
confirm_actions: Сравнить system_time в top_rusage до/после huge_pages=on на НТ
refute_actions: huge_pages=on и страницы зарезервированы — не эта причина
shared_buffers небольшой (<2GB) — эффект HugePages обычно слабый

causes.title: Высокая скорость генерации WAL (wal_bytes)
causes.description: wal_bytes / interval выше порога — общая write-нагрузка.
evidence: [nt1] WAL generation ≈ 19972.4 MB/h
[nt2] WAL generation ≈ 17965.0 MB/h
[nt3] WAL generation ≈ 17457.9 MB/h
confirm_actions: Сравнить WAL MB/h между периодами (compare_runs / compare_nt_prod)
refute_actions: wal_bytes низкий за интервал — симптом мог быть кратковременным вне окна отчёта

causes.title: Переполнение wal_buffers
evidence: [nt1] wal_buffers_full=932205
[nt2] wal_buffers_full=664448

# PostgreSQL User Name Maps
# =========================
#
# Refer to the PostgreSQL documentation, chapter "Client
# Authentication" for a complete description.  A short synopsis
# follows.
#
# This file controls PostgreSQL user name mapping.  It maps external
# user names to their corresponding PostgreSQL user names.  Records
# are of the form:
#
# MAPNAME  SYSTEM-USERNAME  PG-USERNAME
#
# (The uppercase quantities must be replaced by actual values.)
#
# MAPNAME is the (otherwise freely chosen) map name that was used in
# pg_hba.conf.  SYSTEM-USERNAME is the detected user name of the
# client.  PG-USERNAME is the requested PostgreSQL user name.  The
# existence of a record specifies that SYSTEM-USERNAME may connect as
# PG-USERNAME.
#
# If SYSTEM-USERNAME starts with a slash (/), it will be treated as a
# regular expression.  Optionally this can contain a capture (a
# parenthesized subexpression).  The substring matching the capture
# will be substituted for \1 (backslash-one) if present in
# PG-USERNAME.
#
# Multiple maps may be specified in this file and used by pg_hba.conf.
#
# No map names are defined in the default configuration.  If all
# system user names and PostgreSQL user names are the same, you don't
# need anything in this file.
#
# This file is read on server startup and when the postmaster receives
# a SIGHUP signal.  If you edit the file on a running system, you have
# to SIGHUP the postmaster for the changes to take effect.  You can
# use "pg_ctl reload" to do that.

# Put your actual configuration here
# ----------------------------------

# MAPNAME       SYSTEM-USERNAME         PG-USERNAME
